heading: Capital Gains Exemption: Two Adjoining Flats as One Home Under Section 54F
tldr: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) recently ruled on claiming capital gains tax exemption for buying two adjoining flats.
This ruling clarifies that two physically connected flats used as a single residence can be treated as one house.
The exemption applies under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act, 1961, for long-term capital gains from selling assets other than a residential house.
Taxpayers must ensure the flats are genuinely integrated and function as a single dwelling unit.
The Income Tax Department retains the right to verify such claims to prevent misuse.
caption:
Ever wondered if you can save tax when you combine two flats into one big home? Good news! A recent tax ruling says if you genuinely connect two adjoining flats and use them as a single house, you can claim capital gains tax exemption when you sell other assets.
